notes:
Captain: dispatched gpt-6.1-sol high, PGID 172835.
S1. FINAL REVIEW identity, scope, and authority. Reviewed PR #712 at exact HEAD 41364d77956cc759fb43e06e735ea1330719a7f0; gh pr view confirms the same open PR head and main base. Reviewed the WHOLE origin/main...HEAD diff against origin/main 529933db948498e7bbf2239c2fbe1b783f136d19: 11 files, 69 insertions, 15 deletions. Read AGENTS.md including Permanent Test Evidence, docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md, ADR 0020, transition-design section 5.9, live beads eshyra-o9bd.19.6.7.7.2 / .7 / .7.1 and eshyra-o9bd.19.6.7.2, including the USER ADJUSTMENT, Captain design and implementer report. Effective profile: rules-clause-complete within this elapsed-time/capability-guidance scope. refs/beads/state resolves to 9e4bb40c789e3364b1605e7321c1537117a4ca02, generated 2026-09-10, and predates these beads; live bd records govern the review. No repository edits, format/build/verification commands, commits, pushes, GitHub comments or merges were performed. Final git status --porcelain was empty.
S2. Mechanism and acceptance assessment. The principal A2-F2 execution path is repaired: advance_time remains mutates:true and invokes advanceWorldTime with campaign, session, provenance, RNG and rules resolver; only its requiresExplicitAction flag was removed. complete_short_rest and complete_long_rest retain the flag. The registry-derived explicit-action list feeds BOTH buildSystemPrompt (protocol.ts:143,177-183) and the turn auditor (orchestrator.ts:1091), so the carve-out reaches the actual consumer, not merely a static list. The auditor still requires executed state-tool evidence (turnAuditor.ts:186-188); inventory gates remain, and mutating-call staging/attempt rollback remain in orchestrator.ts:993,1229-1230. DM pacing is an authorized owner under the Captain design, so this is not an unowned mutation or a removal of deterministic ownership.

Traced toolRest.ts -> rest.ts:177-253: positive safe-integer minutes, atomic elapsed-clock mutation, expireElapsedWorldEffects, stable character and combatant recovery, then item clock events. Item reset executor processes actual dawn boundaries and anchored resets/timers; generic reset_usage does not replace this path. update_clock only writes the narrative label/stamp and location (domainMutations.ts:1119-1177). Rest completion uses advanceWorldTime once (rest.ts:657-660), returns/persists expiry/recovery/item evidence (674-684), and applies participant rest-item resets (686-695); the NEW rest-tool claims about settling effects, recovery and item events are TRUE. Pact Magic/ordinary-slot distinction and long-rest validation are implemented, not inferred from descriptions.

Independent real-registry probes: Bless declared as 10 rounds is refused because the source duration is 1 minute; a correctly declared Bless remains active through 12 additional combat rounds with elapsed_minutes=0; early end_effect(reason=expired) is refused; advance_time(1) expires it with expired evidence. Ordinary round and participant-turn timers already use their declared combat boundaries/closure (activeEffects.ts:7918 onward and existing regression coverage). No automatic combat-clock advancement is required by the USER ADJUSTMENT. Printed authority checked directly in records.json: rule:the-order-of-combat, SRD p.90, "A round represents about 6 seconds in the game world"; spell:bless p.122, "Concentration, up to 1 minute"; rule:duration p.102. This is a disclosed engine-clock limit, not a claim that SRD combat consumes no fictional time.
S3. MATERIAL finding M1 — new model-facing expiry guidance falsely excludes rest completion. Sibling locations: packages/core/src/orchestrator/protocol.ts:312-313 ("A minute/hour/day effect only expires after elapsed time is passed with advance_time"); packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolStartEffect.ts:54-55 ("Minute/hour/day timers expire only when elapsed time is passed with advance_time"); packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRest.ts:63 ("minute timers expire only after advance_time"). These are tool-name exclusivity claims in the actual DM prompt/tool descriptions. They conflict with both the new TRUE rest descriptions at toolRest.ts:108-109 and the inventory's correctly qualified statement at deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:480 ("advance_time or a rest tool").

Concrete counterexample, independent of the added tests: /tmp/eshyra-pr712-lifecycle-review.mts drives the actual registry against in-memory migrated DBs with the unmodified bundled pack. In EACH of three fresh scenarios it spends a pack-bound Iron Bands of Binding use, closes combat, starts separate 1-minute/1-hour/1-day effects, and damages/stabilizes a second PC. It then invokes ONLY the selected time driver: advance_time(1440), complete_short_rest(durationMinutes=1440, strenuousActivity=false), or complete_long_rest(durationMinutes=1440, sleepMinutes=1320, lightActivityMinutes=120, strenuousInterruptionMinutes=0, foodAndDrink=true), with pc-1 as rest participant. All three return elapsed_minutes=1440, expiredEffects=[minute,hour,day], one stable recovery (deadline=180; pc-2 becomes alive at 1 HP), and one dawn item reset to remaining=1. Neither rest scenario calls the advance_time TOOL. This follows rest.ts:657 calling advanceWorldTime internally, which calls expiry at rest.ts:216. The existing rest.test.ts:810-843 independently proves a 1-hour effect expires during a 60-minute short rest. No live-model guess is needed to falsify the exclusive wording.

Violated invariant/authority: the owning bead requires truthful lifecycle guidance matching the real contracts; its design explicitly says to state exactly what rests do. ADR 0020 section 3 and transition section 5.9 condition 6 require truthful positively selected capability operation/limits. Consequence is an actually false, contradictory contract presented to the DM about which calls can expire effects. I do NOT assert a reproduced double-advancement or model failure. Materiality is to this PR's central model-contract/truthfulness deliverable; the time engine itself is working. SRD source check: rule:duration p.102, "A spell’s duration is the length of time the spell persists"; rule:short-rest p.87, "at least 1 hour long"; rule:long-rest p.87, "at least 8 hours long". The engine honours elapsed rest time; the exclusive tool claim has no SRD authority.

Owner/closure: the .7 repair implementer must qualify ALL three sibling statements to include complete_short_rest/complete_long_rest (or describe expiry as driven by advancement of the elapsed clock, naming all public paths), preserving the disclosure that combat rounds do not automatically advance that clock. No engine rewrite is needed. Permanent evidence should be a generalized model-guidance invariant that keeps the rest paths in the expiry contract; retain the existing runtime rest/time invariants. The /tmp reproducer is diagnostic evidence, not a demand for another costly permanent scenario matrix. Per review policy, this finding requires correction before approval.
S4. Evidence, sibling search, and limits. Targeted execution passed: npx vitest run on packages/core/test/{protocol,tools,itemPerDayDawnEconomy,rest,activeEffects,exhaustion,turnAuditor}.test.ts — 7 files, 366 tests, all passed (23.03s). The original invocation also named a nonexistent turnAuditorInventoryGuard.test.ts; Vitest selected the seven existing files just listed. git diff --check passed. Reviewed the complete added tests: no previous assertions were removed/weakened; the real-pack dawn test now additionally checks an expired timed effect while preserving before-dawn refusal and actual dawn recharge assertions. The protocol and registry tests exercise the newly required routing/gate invariants. Existing rest tests cover due item timers, dawn/rest resets, stable recovery evidence, expiry, and transactional rollback; existing effects tests cover round/participant clocks and closure.

The /tmp probe additionally confirmed minute/hour/day expiry and natural stable recovery through advance_time AND both rest tools with the real pack. records.json authority: Iron Bands of Binding, SRD p.228, "Once the bands are used, they can’t be used again until the next dawn"; Wand of Secrets p.249, "The wand regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn"; Stabilizing a Creature p.98, "A stable creature that isn’t healed regains 1 hit point after 1d4 hours." Checked these against the bounded item/reset and HP implementations rather than treating tests/readiness labels as rules authority.

All 11 changed files and their affected producers/consumers were reviewed. No additional material finding, unowned mutation, weakened regression, new SRD-mechanics contradiction, or new proof infrastructure needing a transition disposition was found in this scope. No separate NON-MATERIAL finding is asserted. A2-F2's omitted time route and explicit-action restriction are fixed operationally; its complete truthful-guidance closure remains blocked by M1. Limits: no full verification run (read-only assignment), no live-model gameplay/auditor experiment, no corpus-wide rules/discovery completeness claim. The tests and probes establish bounded execution and contract evidence, not universal model compliance.

S5. Required next state: correct the three exclusive-expiry statements identified in S3, retain the working rest/advance_time lifecycle and the intentional absence of automatic combat-clock advancement, and review the resulting head. This review does not authorize merge.

VERDICT: MATERIAL FINDINGS (1)
